title: The article discusses misconceptions surrounding Mozambique's fishing industry, particularly the belief that the best fish is exported to the Soviet Union. A report from the Scandinavian aid program MONAP reveals that the joint venture Mosopesca, which includes both Mozambican and Soviet investment, primarily focuses on supplying affordable fish for the local market rather than exporting high-quality fish. The report highlights that while the Soviet Union does have fishing licenses in Mozambique, the majority of prawns are actually exported to Spain. The fishing industry has improved since independence, with a focus on mass production of cheap fish to address nutritional needs, leading to increased local fish consumption. Overall, the fishing sector is portrayed as a success story for Mozambique, contributing to both domestic food security and foreign exchange earnings.
